subject: Career
title: Managing Impressions Without Being Fake
description: Learn Managing Impressions Without Being Fake in one minute.

hook.text: Impression management sounds manipulative. But every job interview, every presentation — it's already happening.

buildup.text: Goffman's dramaturgical theory: social life is a performance. We all manage impressions constantly.

discovery.text: Effective impression management means showing the best version of your real self, not creating a fake one.

twist.text: People who refuse to 'play the game' often get passed over — not because they lack skill, but visibility.

climax.text: Be strategically authentic: share your wins, dress the part, and communicate confidence. It's not fake — it's curated.

punchline.text: Impression management isn't lying. It's editing.

quiz.question: What is impression management according to Goffman?
options: Showing the best version of your real self strategically

details.summary: Impression management involves strategically presenting yourself to influence how others perceive you. Done authentically, it means highlighting genuine strengths and adapting communication style to context rather than fabricating a false persona.
details.whyItMatters: People form impressions of you whether you manage them or not. Intentional impression management ensures those impressions accurately reflect your capabilities and character.
takeaways: Authentic impression management highlights real strengths strategically
Adapt your communication style to the audience without changing your values
Inconsistency between managed impressions and behavior destroys credibility

faq.question: Where is the line between impression management and being fake?
faq.answer: Impression management becomes fake when the image you project contradicts your actual behavior, values, or capabilities. Choosing to emphasize your strategic thinking in a leadership meeting while saving your humor for team lunches is adaptation, not deception.

faq.question: How do you know what impression you are currently making at work?
faq.answer: Ask trusted colleagues directly. Phrases like 'if you had to describe me to someone who had not met me, what would you say' can reveal gaps between your intended impression and your actual one. Three-sixty feedback processes provide more structured insight.
